core_architecture_principles.problem_addressed: Software structure deteriorates when business rules, workflows, and mechanisms are tangled.
forces_and_constraints: Business change is continuous.
Accidental coupling makes safe change expensive.
responsibilities: Keep business rules findable and protected.
Keep mechanisms replaceable.
control_flow: External request enters an adapter, then application orchestration, then domain decisions.
data_flow: DTOs/raw data are translated before reaching domain objects.
core_architecture_principles.transaction_boundary: None by default; transaction boundaries are introduced when state changes must commit atomically.
core_architecture_principles.failure_boundary: Failures should be classified at the boundary that can act on them.
consistency_implications: Layering enables local reasoning but cannot remove all coupling.
testing_strategy: Use unit tests for core logic and integration tests for seams.
benefits: Creates places for business logic and infrastructure to live separately.
costs: Adds structure that may be unnecessary for tiny scripts.
failure_modes: Layers become labels only while dependencies still point everywhere.
use_when: A system has enough business behavior that change is risky.
do_not_use_when: The application is simple CRUD or a short-lived script.
signs_the_pattern_is_needed: Business decisions are hidden in views, ORMs, or adapters.
signs_the_pattern_is_overengineering: The proposed layers have no different responsibilities.
migration_path: Extract one business rule and one adapter seam before large reorganization.
core_architecture_principles.minimal_code_shape: entrypoint -> application service -> domain model -> port/repository -> adapter/infrastructure
